title: A Lesson in Humility
author: James Baldwin
summary: 诗人阿布·阿塔亚提醒哈里发：一切欢乐终将如幻影消散。
publicDomainBasis: Published 1912 by the American Book Company; author James Baldwin (1841–1925). Public domain in the United States and in China (author's life plus 70 years).

paragraphs.en: One day the caliph, Haroun-al-Raschid, made a great feast. The feast was held in the grandest room of the palace. The walls and ceiling glittered with gold and precious gems. The table was decorated with rare and beautiful plants and flowers.
paragraphs.zh: 一天，哈里发哈伦·拉希德举办了一场盛大的宴会。宴会在宫殿最宏伟的厅堂里举行。墙壁和天花板金光闪闪，镶满宝石。桌上装饰着珍稀美丽的花草。

paragraphs.en: All the noblest men of Persia and Arabia were there. Many wise men and poets and musicians had also been invited.
paragraphs.zh: 波斯和阿拉伯所有最尊贵的人都到场了。许多智者、诗人和音乐家也应邀前来。

paragraphs.en: In the midst of the feast the caliph called upon the poet, Abul Atayah, and said, "O prince of verse makers, show us thy skill. Describe in verse this glad and glorious feast."
paragraphs.zh: 宴会进行到一半，哈里发召来诗人阿布·阿塔亚，说：“哦，诗人之王，让我们见识你的本领吧。用诗句描绘这场欢快而辉煌的宴会。”

paragraphs.en: The poet rose and began: "Live, O caliph and enjoy thyself in the shelter of thy lofty palace."
paragraphs.zh: 诗人起身吟道：“愿哈里发长命百岁，在高耸的宫殿庇护下尽情享受。”

paragraphs.en: "That is a good beginning," said Raschid. "Let us hear the rest." The poet went on: "May each morning bring thee some new joy. May each evening see that all thy wishes have been performed."
paragraphs.zh: “开头不错，”拉希德说，“让我们听听后面的。”诗人继续吟道：“愿每个清晨都给你带来新的欢乐，愿每个黄昏都看到你的心愿一一实现。”

paragraphs.en: The poet bowed his head and obeyed: "But when the hour of death comes, O my caliph, then alas! thou wilt learn that all thy delights were but a shadow."
paragraphs.zh: 诗人低下头，遵命吟道：“可是，当死亡降临的时刻到来，哦，我的哈里发，唉！你就会明白，你所有的欢乐不过是一场幻影。”

paragraphs.en: The caliph's eyes were filled with tears. Emotion choked him. He covered his face and wept.
paragraphs.zh: 哈里发眼中含泪，激动得说不出话来。他掩面哭泣。

paragraphs.en: Then one of the officers, who was sitting near the poet, cried out: "Stop! The caliph wished you to amuse him with pleasant thoughts, and you have filled his mind with melancholy."
paragraphs.zh: 这时，坐在诗人旁边的一位官员喊道：“停下！哈里发本想让你用愉快的想法取悦他，你却让他满心忧伤。”

paragraphs.en: "Let the poet alone," said Raschid. "He has seen me in my blindness, and is trying to open my eyes."
paragraphs.zh: “别管这位诗人，”拉希德说，“他看见了我的盲目，正试图让我睁开眼睛。”

paragraphs.en: Haroun-al-Raschid (Aaron the Just) was the greatest of all the caliphs of Bagdad. In a wonderful book, called "The Arabian Nights," there are many interesting stories about him.
paragraphs.zh: 哈伦·拉希德（即“公正的亚伦”）是巴格达所有哈里发中最伟大的一位。在一本名叫《一千零一夜》的奇书里，有许多关于他的有趣故事。
